Outbox relay is claim+lease, not deliver-under-lock: one statement (CTE FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) claims a batch, counts the attempt and leases rows for 300s; delivery (Laravel event + tagged OutboxConsumer) runs outside any transaction, so consumers may do network calls and their own DB writes never commit with a failure mark; a crashed relay's rows return after the lease. Failure: available_at = now()+min(3600, 30*2^(attempts-1)), last_error. No ordering guarantee across retries.

Fingerprint check (TableNames, lazy, once per process) also scans the current schema for other '<prefix>_schema_state' tables whose stored prefix matches their name: a changed prefix hides the own state table, so checking only it could never detect the change. Host tables with similar names are ignored.

CommerzMigration helpers take the Blueprint explicitly ($this->money($table, 'price'), ref($table, 'customer'), uuidPrimary($table), timestampsTz($table)) instead of implicit state; added create()/drop() (create renames PK to {table}_pk via pg_constraint), identityPrimary(), index/unique/foreign with ConstraintNames, check(). money() adds the shared 'currency' char(3) once per table.

TableNames::table() refuses a logical table no SchemaOwnership noun covers (LogicException) as a runtime typo/ownership guard; a noun covers a table equal to it, its plural (Str::plural) or prefixed '{noun}_'; longest noun wins (x_<vendor>). Packages declare nouns via callAfterResolving(SchemaOwnership) so provider order does not matter; core owner id 'commerz.core'.

Added public Commerz\Operations\Fingerprint::of() (sha256 of canonical JSON, map keys sorted, lists ordered) for OperationReceipts fingerprints and the schema fingerprint. commerz:operations:prune also prunes delivered outbox messages with the same TTL (chunked ctid deletes); relay --once drains what is ready, then exits.

All Commerz timestamps are timestamptz(6): Laravel's default precision 0 rounds now() up to the next second, which made fresh outbox rows not yet available (available_at > now()). Later packages should use precision 6 (CommerzMigration::timestampsTz does).
